Do calculations rather than only reading.
"Gauge/Gravity Duality" by Martin Ammon and Johanna Erdmenger,
explain ordinary D-brane AdS/CFT decoupling on a blackboard without notes.
Understand the language of the project
Study BPS decoupling limits, non-Lorentzian limits, Galilean vs Carrollian geometry, longitudinal/transverse directions and Matrix theory basics. Start reading
You can explain exactly what a BPS decoupling limit is, what becomes non-Lorentzian, and why that has anything to do with holography.
Study timelike T-duality, Type II∗, E-branes and their supergravity solutions. Read the 2025 dS/Carrollian-brane Derive the central limits yourself.
Produce your own 5--10 page technical note:
can be used in projectpaper line-by-line.
Give your supervisor a map of
what is known, what is assumed, and what is unclear

Read the newest Blair/Obers/Yan work and important references backwards. Work through the actual Carrollian geometry rather than merely its c→0 slogan. Identify assumptions and gaps in existing constructions.
A sharply formulated thesis question plus one calculation reproduced independently.

Stop broad background reading. Pick one tractable primary direction with your supervisor: E-brane geometry, comparison with AdS limits, Matrix/E-brane description, or a simple Carrollian holographic example. Reproduce the key literature result first.
First genuinely new result, even if small or negative.
Push beyond the paper: modify a limit, investigate an example, derive geometric quantities, compare dual descriptions, or test a proposed holographic dictionary. Keep a daily calculation notebook.
By March 31, know what the principal result of the thesis is likely to be.
Continue the main calculation. Test special cases and consistency limits. Compare with existing literature. Discuss results frequently with supervisor.
Finish outstanding calculations. Decide what is definitely included and what is abandoned. Do not keep opening new research directions indefinitely.
Introduction, background, conventions, D-brane comparison, E-brane/Carroll setup, your calculation/results. Most background can already have been drafted earlier.
Rewrite weak sections, fill derivation gaps, make figures, check signs/factors/conventions and bibliography. Give supervisor a complete document, not isolated chapters.
Incorporate comments. Check every equation you rely on. Make abstract/conclusion accurately distinguish your work from literature.
Formatting, citations, spelling, appendices, compile on another computer, submission requirements.
